passages.text: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, the king’s command and edict were to be executed. On this day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, but their plan was overturned and the Jews overpowered those who hated them.
passages.sermon:
The Jews lived in the kingdom of King Xerxes.
The king gave a command and an edict.
The command and edict were to be carried out on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month.
The twelfth month is called Adar.
On this day, the enemies of the Jews hoped to rule over the Jews.
The plan of the enemies did not succeed.
The situation was reversed.
The Jews overpowered those who hated them.
passages.original: וּבִשְׁנֵים֩ עָשָׂ֨ר חֹ֜דֶשׁ הוּא־ חֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֗ר בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ בּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִגִּ֧יעַ דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְדָת֖וֹ לְהֵעָשׂ֑וֹת בַּיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שִׂבְּר֜וּ אֹיְבֵ֤י הַיְּהוּדִים֙ לִשְׁל֣וֹט בָּהֶ֔ם וְנַהֲפ֣וֹךְ ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלְט֧וּ הַיְּהוּדִ֛ים הֵ֖מָּה בְּשֹׂנְאֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: In each of the provinces of King Xerxes, the Jews assembled in their cities to attack those who sought to harm them. No man could withstand them, because the fear of them had fallen upon all peoples.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled many provinces.
The Jews lived in these provinces.
The Jews gathered together in their cities.
They gathered to attack those who wanted to harm them.
No one could stand against the Jews.
All the peoples were afraid of the Jews.
passages.original: נִקְהֲל֨וּ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים בְּעָרֵיהֶ֗ם בְּכָל־ מְדִינוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֳחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ יָ֔ד בִּמְבַקְשֵׁ֖י רָֽעָתָ֑ם וְאִישׁ֙ לֹא־ עָמַ֣ד לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־ נָפַ֥ל פַּחְדָּ֖ם עַל־ כָּל־ הָעַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: And all the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and the king’s administrators helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a powerful Jewish leader in the Persian Empire.
He served in the palace of King Xerxes.
All the officials of the provinces helped the Jews.
The satraps helped the Jews.
The governors helped the Jews.
The king’s administrators helped the Jews.
They helped the Jews because they feared Mordecai.
The fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them.
passages.original: וְכָל־ שָׂרֵ֨י הַמְּדִינ֜וֹת וְהָאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִ֣ים וְהַפַּח֗וֹת וְעֹשֵׂ֤י הַמְּלָאכָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מְנַשְּׂאִ֖ים אֶת־ הַיְּהוּדִ֑ים כִּֽי־ נָפַ֥ל פַּֽחַד־ מָרְדֳּכַ֖י עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For Mordecai exercised great power in the palace, and his fame spread throughout the provinces as he became more and more powerful.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai lived in the palace of King Xerxes.
Mordecai became very important in the king’s palace.
People in every province heard about Mordecai.
Mordecai’s fame spread everywhere.
Mordecai kept growing in power.
Mordecai became greater and greater.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ גָ֤דוֹל מָרְדֳּכַי֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְשָׁמְע֖וֹ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּכָל־ הַמְּדִינ֑וֹת כִּֽי־ הָאִ֥ישׁ מָרְדֳּכַ֖י הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֽוֹל׃פ

passages.text: The Jews put all their enemies to the sword, killing and destroying them, and they did as they pleased to those who hated them.
passages.sermon:
The Jews fought against all their enemies.
They struck their enemies with the sword.
They killed their enemies.
They destroyed their enemies.
They did whatever they wanted to those who hated them.
passages.original: וַיַּכּ֤וּ הַיְּהוּדִים֙ בְּכָל־ אֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם מַכַּת־ חֶ֥רֶב וְהֶ֖רֶג וְאַבְדָ֑ן וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְשֹׂנְאֵיהֶ֖ם כִּרְצוֹנָֽם׃

passages.text: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men, including Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
passages.sermon:
The Jews lived in the citadel of Susa.
The Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men there.
They killed Parshandatha.
They killed Dalphon.
They killed Aspatha.
They killed Poratha.
They killed Adalia.
They killed Aridatha.
They killed Parmashta.
They killed Arisai.
They killed Aridai.
They killed Vaizatha.
passages.original: וּבְשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֗ה הָרְג֤וּ הַיְּהוּדִים֙ וְאַבֵּ֔ד חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃ וְאֵ֧ת׀ פַּרְשַׁנְדָּ֛תָא וְאֵ֥ת׀ דַּֽלְפ֖וֹן וְאֵ֥ת׀ אַסְפָּֽתָא׃ וְאֵ֧ת׀ פּוֹרָ֛תָא וְאֵ֥ת׀ אֲדַלְיָ֖א וְאֵ֥ת׀ אֲרִידָֽתָא׃ וְאֵ֤ת׀ פַּרְמַ֙שְׁתָּא֙ וְאֵ֣ת׀ אֲרִיסַ֔י וְאֵ֥ת׀ אֲרִדַ֖י וְאֵ֥ת׀ וַיְזָֽתָא׃

passages.text: They killed these ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
passages.sermon:
The Jews had an enemy named Haman.
Haman was the son of Hammedatha.
Haman hated the Jews.
The Jews killed Haman’s ten sons.
The Jews did not take any plunder.
passages.original: עֲ֠שֶׂרֶת בְּנֵ֨י הָמָ֧ן בֶּֽן־ הַמְּדָ֛תָא צֹרֵ֥ר הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים הָרָ֑גוּ וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־ יָדָֽם׃

passages.text: On that day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king, who said to Queen Esther, “In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men, including Haman’s ten sons. What have they done in the rest of the royal provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be given to you. And what further do you request? It will be fulfilled.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Persia ruled over many provinces.
Queen Esther was his wife.
The Jews lived in the citadel of Susa.
On that day, someone reported to the king.
They told him how many people had been killed in Susa.
The king spoke to Queen Esther.
He said, “In the citadel of Susa, the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men.
They also killed the ten sons of Haman.
Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
What have the Jews done in the other royal provinces?
What is your petition, Queen Esther?
It will be given to you.
What further request do you have?
It will be fulfilled.”
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא בָּ֣א מִסְפַּ֧ר הַֽהֲרוּגִ֛ים בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֗ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֡ה הָרְגוּ֩ הַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְאַבֵּ֜ד חֲמֵ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ וְאֵת֙ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת בְּנֵֽי־ הָמָ֔ן בִּשְׁאָ֛ר מְדִינ֥וֹת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ וּמַה־ שְּׁאֵֽלָתֵךְ֙ וְיִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֔ךְ וּמַה־ בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃

passages.text: Esther replied, “If it pleases the king, may the Jews in Susa also have tomorrow to carry out today’s edict, and may the bodies of Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”
passages.sermon:
Esther was the queen.
Esther spoke to the king.
Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa have permission for tomorrow."
She asked that the Jews in Susa could do as the law allowed today.
She also asked that the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶסְתֵּר֙ אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב יִנָּתֵ֣ן גַּם־ מָחָ֗ר לַיְּהוּדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשׁוּשָׁ֔ן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כְּדָ֣ת הַיּ֑וֹם וְאֵ֛ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת בְּנֵֽי־ הָמָ֖ן יִתְל֥וּ עַל־ הָעֵֽץ׃

passages.text: So the king commanded that this be done. An edict was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
passages.sermon:
The king gave a command.
He ordered that Esther’s request be fulfilled.
The officials issued an edict in Susa.
They hanged the ten sons of Haman.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְהֵֽעָשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן וַתִּנָּתֵ֥ן דָּ֖ת בְּשׁוּשָׁ֑ן וְאֵ֛ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת בְּנֵֽי־ הָמָ֖ן תָּלֽוּ׃

passages.text: On the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, the Jews in Susa came together again and put to death three hundred men there, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
passages.sermon:
The Jews lived in Susa.
Susa was the capital city.
On the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, the Jews in Susa gathered together again.
They killed three hundred men in Susa.
They did not take any of the plunder.
passages.original: וַיִּֽקָּהֲל֞וּ הַיְּהוּדִיִּים אֲשֶׁר־ בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן גַּ֠ם בְּי֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר וַיַּֽהַרְג֣וּ בְשׁוּשָׁ֔ן שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־ יָדָֽם׃

passages.text: The rest of the Jews in the royal provinces also assembled to defend themselves and rid themselves of their enemies. They killed 75,000 who hated them, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
passages.sermon:
The Jews lived in the royal provinces.
They gathered together.
They defended themselves.
They found relief from their enemies.
They killed 75,000 people who hated them.
They did not take any plunder.
passages.original: וּשְׁאָ֣ר הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ בִּמְדִינ֨וֹת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ נִקְהֲל֣וּ׀ וְעָמֹ֣ד עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְנ֙וֹחַ֙ מֵאֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָרֹג֙ בְּשֹׂ֣נְאֵיהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָֽׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־ יָדָֽם׃

passages.text: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth day they rested, making it a day of feasting and joy.
passages.sermon:
The Jews acted on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar.
They finished their actions on that day.
On the fourteenth day of Adar, the Jews rested.
They made the fourteenth day a day of feasting.
They made the fourteenth day a day of joy.
passages.original: בְּיוֹם־ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֑ר וְנ֗וֹחַ בְּאַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וְעָשֹׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ י֖וֹם מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה וְשִׂמְחָֽה׃

passages.text: The Jews in Susa, however, had assembled on the thirteenth and the fourteenth days of the month. So they rested on the fifteenth day, making it a day of feasting and joy.
passages.sermon:
The Jews lived in Susa.
They gathered together on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar.
They also gathered on the fourteenth day of Adar.
They rested on the fifteenth day of Adar.
They made the fifteenth day a day of feasting.
They made it a day of joy.
passages.original: וְהַיְּהוּדִיִּים אֲשֶׁר־ בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן נִקְהֲלוּ֙ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וּבְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר בּ֑וֹ וְנ֗וֹחַ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וְעָשֹׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ י֖וֹם מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה וְשִׂמְחָֽה׃

passages.text: This is why the rural Jews, who live in the villages, observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of joy and feasting. It is a holiday for sending gifts to one another.
passages.sermon:
The rural Jews live in the villages.
They observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar.
They make this day a day of joy.
They make this day a day of feasting.
They treat this day as a holiday.
They send gifts to one another on this day.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֞ן הַיְּהוּדִ֣ים הַפְּרוֹזִים הַיֹּשְׁבִים֮ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַפְּרָזוֹת֒ עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֠ת י֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר שִׂמְחָ֥ה וּמִשְׁתֶּ֖ה וְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב וּמִשְׁל֥וֹחַ מָנ֖וֹת אִ֥ישׁ לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃פ

passages.text: Mordecai recorded these events and sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Xerxes, both near and far, to establish among them an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar as the days on which the Jews gained rest from their enemies and the month in which their sorrow turned to joy and their mourning into a holiday. He wrote that these were to be days of feasting and joy, of sending gifts to one another and to the poor.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a leader among the Jews.
He wrote down everything that had happened.
He sent letters to all the Jews.
These Jews lived in every province of King Xerxes.
Some Jews lived close by.
Some Jews lived far away.
Mordecai told them to celebrate every year.
They must celebrate on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar.
These days were when the Jews found rest from their enemies.
This month was when their sorrow became joy.
Their mourning turned into a holiday.
Mordecai said these days must be days of feasting and joy.
They must send gifts to each other.
They must also give gifts to the poor.
passages.original: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מָרְדֳּכַ֔י אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סְפָרִ֜ים אֶל־ כָּל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּכָל־ מְדִינוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ הַקְּרוֹבִ֖ים וְהָרְחוֹקִֽים׃ לְקַיֵּם֮ עֲלֵיהֶם֒ לִהְי֣וֹת עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֠ת י֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר וְאֵ֛ת יוֹם־ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר בּ֑וֹ בְּכָל־ שָׁנָ֖ה וְשָׁנָֽה׃ כַּיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־ נָ֨חוּ בָהֶ֤ם הַיְּהוּדִים֙ מֵא֣וֹיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וְהַחֹ֗דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר֩ נֶהְפַּ֨ךְ לָהֶ֤ם מִיָּגוֹן֙ לְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּמֵאֵ֖בֶל לְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אוֹתָ֗ם יְמֵי֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה וְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּמִשְׁל֤וֹחַ מָנוֹת֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּמַתָּנ֖וֹת לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: So the Jews agreed to continue the custom they had started, as Mordecai had written to them.
passages.sermon:
The Jews are the people of Israel.
They began a new custom.
They agreed to keep doing this custom.
Mordecai wrote instructions to them.
The Jews accepted what Mordecai wrote.
passages.original: וְקִבֵּל֙ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ הֵחֵ֖לּוּ לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ כָּתַ֥ב מָרְדֳּכַ֖י אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the Pur (that is, the lot) to crush and destroy them.
passages.sermon:
Haman was the son of Hammedatha.
Haman was an Agagite.
Haman was the enemy of all the Jews.
Haman planned to destroy the Jews.
Haman cast the Pur, which means the lot.
Haman used the lot to decide when to crush and destroy the Jews.
passages.original: כִּי֩ הָמָ֨ן בֶּֽן־ הַמְּדָ֜תָא הָֽאֲגָגִ֗י צֹרֵר֙ כָּל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים חָשַׁ֥ב עַל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים לְאַבְּדָ֑ם וְהִפִּ֥יל פּוּר֙ ה֣וּא הַגּוֹרָ֔ל לְהֻמָּ֖ם וּֽלְאַבְּדָֽם׃

passages.text: But when it came before the king, he commanded by letter that the wicked scheme which Haman had devised against the Jews should come back upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
passages.sermon:
Esther was the queen.
Esther came before the king.
She brought the matter to the king’s attention.
Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
Haman had planned evil against the Jews.
The king gave a command in writing.
The king ordered that Haman’s wicked plan would return on Haman’s own head.
The king ordered that Haman and his sons be hanged on the gallows.
passages.original: וּבְבֹאָהּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ אָמַ֣ר עִם־ הַסֵּ֔פֶר יָשׁ֞וּב מַחֲשַׁבְתּ֧וֹ הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ חָשַׁ֥ב עַל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וְתָל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֖יו עַל־ הָעֵֽץ׃

passages.text: Therefore these days are called Purim, from the word Pur. Because of all the instructions in this letter, and because of all they had seen and experienced, the Jews bound themselves to establish the custom that they and their descendants and all who join them should not fail to celebrate these two days at the appointed time each and every year, according to their regulation.
passages.sermon:
The Jews gave these days a name.
They called them Purim.
They chose this name because of the word "Pur."
"Pur" means "lot."
Haman cast lots to decide the fate of the Jews.
The Jews remembered all the instructions in the letter.
They remembered everything they saw and experienced.
The Jews made a promise.
They promised to keep this custom.
They bound themselves to celebrate these two days every year.
They included their descendants in this promise.
They included everyone who joined them.
They promised never to stop celebrating these days.
They agreed to keep the celebration at the set time each year.
They agreed to follow the written rules for these days.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֡ן קָֽרְאוּ֩ לַיָּמִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה פוּרִים֙ עַל־ שֵׁ֣ם הַפּ֔וּר עַל־ כֵּ֕ן עַל־ כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֖י הָאִגֶּ֣רֶת הַזֹּ֑את וּמָֽה־ רָא֣וּ עַל־ כָּ֔כָה וּמָ֥ה הִגִּ֖יעַ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ קִיְּמ֣וּ וְקִבֵּל הַיְּהוּדִים֩׀ עֲלֵיהֶ֨ם׀ וְעַל־ זַרְעָ֜ם וְעַ֨ל כָּל־ הַנִּלְוִ֤ים עֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲב֔וֹר לִהְי֣וֹת עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י הַיָּמִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה כִּכְתָבָ֖ם וְכִזְמַנָּ֑ם בְּכָל־ שָׁנָ֖ה וְשָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: These days should be remembered and celebrated by every generation, family, province, and city, so that these days of Purim should not fail to be observed among the Jews, nor should the memory of them fade from their descendants.
passages.sermon:
The Jews celebrate the days of Purim.
They remember these days in every generation.
Every family remembers these days.
Every province remembers these days.
Every city remembers these days.
The Jews do not stop observing the days of Purim.
Their descendants do not forget the memory of these days.
passages.original: וְהַיָּמִ֣ים הָ֠אֵלֶּה נִזְכָּרִ֨ים וְנַעֲשִׂ֜ים בְּכָל־ דּ֣וֹר וָד֗וֹר מִשְׁפָּחָה֙ וּמִשְׁפָּחָ֔ה מְדִינָ֥ה וּמְדִינָ֖ה וְעִ֣יר וָעִ֑יר וִימֵ֞י הַפּוּרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה לֹ֤א יַֽעַבְרוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְזִכְרָ֖ם לֹא־ יָס֥וּף מִזַּרְעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: So Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.
passages.sermon:
Queen Esther was the daughter of Abihail.
Mordecai was a Jew.
Queen Esther and Mordecai acted together.
They wrote with full authority.
They confirmed the second letter about Purim.
passages.original: וַ֠תִּכְתֹּב אֶסְתֵּ֨ר הַמַּלְכָּ֧ה בַת־ אֲבִיחַ֛יִל וּמָרְדֳּכַ֥י הַיְּהוּדִ֖י אֶת־ כָּל־ תֹּ֑קֶף לְקַיֵּ֗ם אֵ֣ת אִגֶּ֧רֶת הַפּוּרִ֛ים הַזֹּ֖את הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

passages.text: And Mordecai sent letters with words of peace and truth to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Xerxes, in order to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed time, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established them and had committed themselves and their descendants to the times of fasting and lamentation.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
Queen Esther was also a Jew.
Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews.
He sent these letters to every province in the kingdom of Xerxes.
There were 127 provinces in this kingdom.
The letters contained words of peace and truth.
Mordecai wanted to confirm the days of Purim.
He wanted the Jews to keep these days at their appointed time.
Mordecai and Queen Esther had already established these days.
They had committed themselves and their descendants to these days.
They also committed to times of fasting and lamentation.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סְפָרִ֜ים אֶל־ כָּל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֶל־ שֶׁ֨בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּמֵאָה֙ מְדִינָ֔ה מַלְכ֖וּת אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ דִּבְרֵ֥י שָׁל֖וֹם וֶאֱמֶֽת׃ לְקַיֵּ֡ם אֵת־ יְמֵי֩ הַפֻּרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ קִיַּ֨ם עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם מָרְדֳּכַ֤י הַיְּהוּדִי֙ וְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֛ר קִיְּמ֥וּ עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖ם וְעַל־ זַרְעָ֑ם דִּבְרֵ֥י הַצֹּמ֖וֹת וְזַעֲקָתָֽם׃

passages.text: So Esther’s decree confirmed these regulations about Purim, which were written into the record.
passages.sermon: Queen Esther made a decree.\r\nShe confirmed the rules about Purim.\r\nThey wrote these rules in the official record.
passages.original: וּמַאֲמַ֣ר אֶסְתֵּ֔ר קִיַּ֕ם דִּבְרֵ֥י הַפֻּרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְנִכְתָּ֖ב בַּסֵּֽפֶר׃פ
